small_guidance:
- The clamp/div epilogue is already trivial; further tuning of BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps on it won't move the needle since ConvTranspose3d dominates. If staying small, at minimum fuse the epilogue into the conv output write and switch the model to `channels_last_3d` so the conv kernel itself runs faster.
- Try setting `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True` and pre-warming so cuDNN picks the best ConvTranspose3d algorithm, and cast weights to channels_last_3d in `__init__`.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per `(N, IC tile, input-spatial tile)`, computing the outer product `input_tile × weight[ic, :, kd, kh, kw]` and atomically scattering into the output grid at `(n, oc, d*stride - pad + kd, h*stride - pad + kh, w*stride - pad + kw)`. Fuse bias add, clamp(min), and division into the scatter epilogue so no second pass is needed.
- Alternative (likely faster, no atomics): gather-style — one program per `(N, OC tile, output-spatial tile)`. For each output voxel `(od, oh, ow)`, iterate `(kd, kh, kw)`; valid input coordinate is `((od + pad - kd)/stride, ...)` only when divisible by stride. Accumulate `sum_ic input[n,ic,id,ih,iw] * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` as a GEMM over IC. Fuse bias + clamp + 1/divisor into the epilogue write.
- Use channels_last_3d layout so the IC reduction axis is contiguous, autotune `BLOCK_OC ∈ {32,64}`, `BLOCK_SPATIAL ∈ {32,64,128}`, `BLOCK_IC ∈ {16,32,64}`, `num_warps ∈ {4,8}`, `num_stages ∈ {2,3}`. Precompute and hoist the `(od+pad-kd) % stride == 0` masks outside the IC loop.
